title: Composite Weil data and the inverse-purity counit calculation
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Use the small pro-etale categories $D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ of [def-pur-conventions], for $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$: integral coefficients are completed and derived complete with uniform cohomological and Tor intervals, and field coefficients are scalar-localized/common-stage objects. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated finite type between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with smooth geometric base change $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$. Write $G_T=Lg_{T,\gamma}^*$, $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$, for [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. For any input $N$ on the target of a morphism under consideration, use strict data in the sense of [def-pur-tate-datum] and the following notation, with the morphism and its dimension substituted as appropriate. Write $P_fN=Lf^*N(d)[2d]$, $F_f=Rf_!$, $E_f=Rf^!$, $a_{f,N}=\gamma_{f,N}:P_fN\simeq E_fN$ for the purity map of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] and its specified coefficient transports [sk-thm-purity-transport], $\epsilon_{f,N}:F_fE_fN\to N$ for the counit of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and $t_{f,N}:F_fP_fN\to N$ for [def-pur-smooth-trace] and its coefficient transports. Use the source and exceptional data of [def-pur-tate-datum] and the compact-support datum $\varphi_{F_fM}=F_f(\varphi_M)e_{f,M}$ of [def-pur-compact-support-transport], where $e_f:G_YF_f\simeq F_fG_X$ is its specified semilinear exchange. All objects below are restricted to the constructible finite-Tor domains of these operations and comparisons.

Let $h_0:Y_0\to Z_0$ be separated finite type, with $Z_0$ separated finite type over $k_0$ and smooth geometric base change $h:Y\to Z$ of pure relative dimension $e\geq0$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$ carry a strict datum $\varphi_K:G_ZK\simeq K$, and use the preceding notation for $h$, $f$, and $hf$ with their corresponding inputs. Use the canonical pullback/twist identification $P_{hf}\simeq P_fP_h$, compact-support composition $\alpha_{h,f}:F_hF_f\simeq F_{hf}$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition], and exceptional composition $c_{h,f}:E_{hf}\simeq E_fE_h$ of [def-pur-composition-comparisons] at finite coefficients and its specified transports. The source identification intertwines the strict data, with twist $\tau_d\otimes Lf^*\tau_e=\tau_{d+e}$; this is the composition clause of [lem-pur-weil-tate-datum-transport]. The actual purity and trace maps satisfy, under that source identification,
$$a_{hf,K}=c_{h,f,K}^{-1}a_{f,E_hK}P_f(a_{h,K}),\quad a_{hf,K}^{-1}=P_f(a_{h,K}^{-1})a_{f,E_hK}^{-1}c_{h,f,K},$$
$$t_{hf,K}\alpha_{h,f,P_{hf}K}=t_{h,K}F_h(t_{f,P_hK}),$$
where the source of the last equality is identified with $F_hF_fP_fP_hK$. In particular the first trace is evaluated at $P_hK= Lh^*K(e)[2e]$. Naturality at $a_{h,K}^{-1}$ has the typed form
$$t_{f,P_hK}F_fP_f(a_{h,K}^{-1})=a_{h,K}^{-1}t_{f,E_hK}.$$
For each of the three morphisms put $\varphi_{E_fN}=a_{f,N}\varphi_{P_fN}(G_Xa_{f,N})^{-1}$ and $\epsilon_{f,N}=t_{f,N}F_f(a_{f,N}^{-1})$, with the analogous conventions on $Y,Z$. Then $c_{h,f,K}$ intertwines $\varphi_{E_{hf}K}$ with the iterated exceptional datum on $E_fE_hK$, and the actual counits obey
$$\epsilon_{hf,K}\alpha_{h,f,E_{hf}K}=\epsilon_{h,K}F_h(\epsilon_{f,E_hK})F_hF_f(c_{h,f,K})$$
$$=t_{h,K}F_h(a_{h,K}^{-1})F_h\bigl(t_{f,E_hK}F_f(a_{f,E_hK}^{-1})\bigr)F_hF_f(c_{h,f,K}).$$
This is the counit of the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] under $c$ and $\alpha$. For the purity sources and exceptional targets, $\alpha$ also intertwines the iterated compact-support data with the datum for $hf$, using the specified vertical-pasting semilinear exchange of [lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing]. Thus these identities identify all labelled arrows in the pasted geometric purity, trace and counit diagrams with their composite-morphism arrows. At integral coefficients they concern the realized strict-tower maps; at field coefficients their localized/common-stage images.

proof.text: The hypotheses give separated finite-type geometric schemes and smooth maps $f,h,hf$, the last of dimension $d+e$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. Use [sk-thm-purity-transport] for the natural isomorphisms $a_f,a_h,a_{hf}$. In the exceptional datum of [def-pur-tate-datum], substitute its prescribed exchange $a_{f,G_YN}b_{f,N}(G_Xa_{f,N})^{-1}$. Naturality gives $E_f(\varphi_N)a_{f,G_YN}=a_{f,N}P_f(\varphi_N)$, hence $\varphi_{E_fN}=a_{f,N}\varphi_{P_fN}(G_Xa_{f,N})^{-1}$. At finite coefficients [def-pur-smooth-trace] gives $t_{f,N}=\epsilon_{f,N}F_f(a_{f,N})$, so cancellation gives $\epsilon_{f,N}=t_{f,N}F_f(a_{f,N}^{-1})$. The same formulas hold for $h,hf$. The counit-preserving purity transport of [sk-thm-purity-transport] gives the same recovery at the other stages.

source.place: Constituent compatibility assembly: identify actual exceptional data and counits before composition

proof.text: At $A_{E,n}$ apply [thm-pur-composition-coherence] with $g=h$ and the comparisons of [def-pur-composition-comparisons]. It gives $c_{h,f,K}a_{hf,K}=a_{f,E_hK}P_f(a_{h,K})$. Apply [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] at the same input $K$: $t_{hf,K}\alpha_{h,f,P_{hf}K}=t_{h,K}F_h(t_{f,P_hK})$. Its inner input is $P_hK$, including $(e)[2e]$. For completed integral coefficients [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence] transports these purity/trace composition equations as coherent tower maps, and [lem-pur-transport-integral-counit-realization] identifies the realized maps with the specified actual family, including uniformizer reductions. At field coefficients [prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence] gives their rationalized/common-stage images. Thus these two equations concern the specified transformations at every stage, rather than equality inferred from finite evaluations.

source.place: Constituent purity and trace composition, with specified coefficient transports

proof.text: Put $A=a_{f,E_hK}$, $B=P_f(a_{h,K})$, and $c=c_{h,f,K}$. Step 2 says $a_{hf,K}=c^{-1}AB$. Multiply on either side to check that $B^{-1}A^{-1}c$ is its inverse: the two products cancel successively $BB^{-1}$, $AA^{-1}$ and $c^{-1}c$, or these pairs in reverse order. Since a functor preserves inverse pairs, $B^{-1}=P_f(a_{h,K}^{-1})$. This proves the inverse-purity identity with exactly its stated order of factors.

source.place: Inverse-purity cancellation in the composite diagram

proof.text: By [lem-pur-weil-tate-datum-transport] the source comparison $P_{hf}K\simeq P_fP_hK$ carries the datum to its iterated source datum $w$, and its twist is $\tau_d\otimes Lf^*\tau_e=\tau_{d+e}$. Keep this comparison inserted throughout. The source formula of [def-pur-tate-datum] is functorial in a datum: if $v'=u v(G_Yu)^{-1}$, substitute this expression into $(Lf^*v'\otimes\tau_d)[2d]b$ and use naturality of $b$ to obtain $\varphi_{P_f(N')}=P_f(u)\varphi_{P_fN}(G_XP_f(u))^{-1}$. Take $u=a_{h,K}$ and use Step 1; thus the source datum on $P_fE_hK$ is $B w(G_XB)^{-1}$. Its exceptional transport is $A B w(G_X(AB))^{-1}$. On the other hand Step 1 gives $\varphi_{E_{hf}K}=a_{hf,K}w(G_Xa_{hf,K})^{-1}$. Substitution of $AB=c a_{hf,K}$ proves $c\varphi_{E_{hf}K}=\varphi_{E_fE_hK}G_X(c)$ by inverse cancellation. This is the asserted exceptional-data intertwining.

source.place: Composition of source data followed by conjugation to exceptional targets

proof.text: By Step 1, at every coefficient stage $t_{f,N}=\epsilon_{f,N}F_f(a_{f,N})$, where $\epsilon_f$ is the counit of the adjunction $F_f\dashv E_f$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (with its specified transports) and $a_f$ is the natural isomorphism of functors of [sk-thm-purity-transport]. A composite of natural transformations is natural, so $t_f:F_fP_f\to\mathrm{id}$ is natural on the constructible finite-Tor category. Apply this to the arrow $a_{h,K}^{-1}:E_hK\to P_hK$: $t_{f,P_hK}F_fP_f(a_{h,K}^{-1})=\epsilon_{f,P_hK}F_fE_f(a_{h,K}^{-1})F_f(a_{f,E_hK})=a_{h,K}^{-1}\epsilon_{f,E_hK}F_f(a_{f,E_hK})=a_{h,K}^{-1}t_{f,E_hK}$, using naturality of $a_f$ and then of $\epsilon_f$. Both $E_hK$ and $P_hK$ lie in the named domains since $P_hK\simeq E_hK$ by purity. This is the typed naturality equation needed below.

source.place: Naturality at inverse purity, retaining the inner Tate twist

proof.text:
Naturality of $\alpha$ at $a_{hf,K}^{-1}$ and Step 1 give
$$\epsilon_{hf,K}\alpha_{E_{hf}K}=t_{hf,K}\alpha_{P_{hf}K}F_hF_f(a_{hf,K}^{-1}).$$
Substitute Steps 2 and 3 and combine consecutive functor images:
$$=t_{h,K}F_h\bigl(t_{f,P_hK}F_fP_f(a_{h,K}^{-1})F_f(a_{f,E_hK}^{-1})\bigr)F_hF_f(c).$$
Step 5 changes this to
$$=t_{h,K}F_h(a_{h,K}^{-1})F_h\bigl(t_{f,E_hK}F_f(a_{f,E_hK}^{-1})\bigr)F_hF_f(c).$$
Step 1 identifies the first two factors and the parenthesized pair, giving $\epsilon_{h,K}F_h(\epsilon_{f,E_hK})F_hF_f(c)$. Naturality used here is the defining naturality of the compact-support composition isomorphism of [thm-sf-comp-composition], with the specified coefficient transports from Step 2. The calculation proves both displayed counit equalities, without cancelling any noninvertible trace.

source.place: Pasted counit: expand, substitute inverse purity, apply trace naturality, cancel

proof.text: The counit formula in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], for $F=F_f,G=E_f,H=F_h,I=E_h$, is exactly $\epsilon_hF_h(\epsilon_f E_h)$. Therefore Step 6 identifies the pasted counit with that composite-adjunction counit through $c$ and $\alpha$. This is a substitution into the definition, not a different choice of counit or compositor.

source.place: Identification with the specified composite adjunction

proof.text:
Write $e_f:G_YF_f\simeq F_fG_X$ and $e_h:G_ZF_h\simeq F_hG_Y$. Vertical-composition compatibility in [lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing] gives
$$e_{hf,M}G_Z(\alpha_M)=\alpha_{G_XM}F_h(e_{f,M})e_{h,F_fM}.$$
For the datum of [def-pur-compact-support-transport], naturality of $\alpha$ then gives
$$\begin{aligned}\varphi_{F_{hf}M}G_Z(\alpha_M)&=F_{hf}(\varphi_M)\alpha_{G_XM}F_h(e_{f,M})e_{h,F_fM}\\&=\alpha_MF_hF_f(\varphi_M)F_h(e_{f,M})e_{h,F_fM}\\&=\alpha_MF_h(\varphi_{F_fM})e_{h,F_fM}.\end{aligned}$$
This proves the compact-support assertion for $M=P_{hf}K,E_{hf}K$ and their identified iterated versions. The cited exchange lemma includes actual strict-tower formation and localized/common-stage transport. Together with Step 4 and the arrow identities of Steps 2--7, this identifies every labelled arrow of the pasted diagrams at all four coefficient stages.
